# Test fixtures

## `known-good-9.1.0-three-node-vsan-esa.json`

A working three-node vSAN ESA VCF spec, vendored from
`lamw/vcf-91-in-box` (`config/three-node-vsan-esa.json`).

**Read this before using it as a reference.**

It is **`version: 9.1.0.0`; this package targets 9.1.1.0.** It fails our
vendored 9.1.1 schema in eight places — `networkSpecs[*].vlanId`,
`nsxtSpec.transportVlanId` and `nsxtSpec.vpcSpec.dtgwSpec.vlan` are strings
where 9.1.1 declares integers, and `dvsSpecs[0].lagSpecs` and
`nsxTeamings[0].standByUplinks` are `null` where arrays are declared. It also
carries three fields 9.1.1 does not declare at all, including
`fleetLcmSpec.hostname` and `sddcLcmSpec.hostname` (those definitions are
`size`/`version` only in 9.1.1).

So it is **not** a structural target, and "render something equivalent to this"
is not a satisfiable acceptance test. Use it to see how a working spec is
shaped, and check every field against
`vcfspec/schemas/9.1.1.0/sddc-spec.schema.json` before copying it.

**Its extra sections are not requirements.** It carries `vcfOperationsSpec`,
`licenseServerSpec`, `vidbSpec` and others that we do not render. A real VCF
9.1.1 Installer was asked to validate our spec without them on 2026-09-21 and
raised **no error** — it reports `AUTOGENERATED_*` notices and supplies them
itself. An earlier design document claimed the opposite and has been retracted;
see `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-21-vcf-deployable-spec-design.md`.

**What it did legitimately reveal:** vMotion and vSAN carry
`includeIpAddressRanges` and our spec did not. That one is real — the Installer
rejects a spec without them — and is now enforced by
`VCF-NET-IP-POOL-MISSING` / `VCF-NET-IP-POOL-TOO-SMALL`.
